html:
The Saraguro are a Kichwa-speaking Indigenous people of the southern highlands of Ecuador, around the town of Saraguro in Loja province. They are known for their black wool clothing and silver jewellery.

A strong tradition says their ancestors were mitmaq, colonists moved here by the Inca Empire from the far south, perhaps the Lake Titicaca region, to hold newly conquered land. Whether or not that is so, they kept a distinct identity through Spanish rule. They farm and raise cattle, and many now also work abroad. They speak Kichwa, a form of Quechua. North of them live the Puruhá.
